event.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuation of Nearly 12,000 Tourists in Southwest France
event.canonical_title: Wildfire Forces Evacuation of Nearly 12,000 Tourists in Southwest France
event.summary: A wildfire in Le Porge, southwest France, has led to the evacuation of nearly 12,000 people, primarily tourists. The fire, which began around midday on Wednesday, has prompted a significant response from hundreds of firefighters battling the flames. The region has been experiencing extreme heat, contributing to the wildfire's rapid spread.

timeline.title: Spain Lifts Wildfire Emergency as France Cools and Supports Evacuees
timeline.summary: Spain has lifted its national emergency status due to wildfires that threatened areas near Madrid, as temperatures have cooled in France, particularly around Bordeaux. In response to the wildfires, a veterinary team in Bordeaux is providing care for pets belonging to evacuees, offering food and medical support while families await their return home.

The situation is part of a broader pattern of wildfires affecting Spain and France, leading to widespread evacuations.

event_overview.title: About Southwest France Wildfire
event_overview.subject: Southwest France Wildfire
event_overview.summary: The Southwest France wildfire was a major late-July 2026 forest-fire emergency in Gironde, west of Bordeaux, affecting the wooded Atlantic-coast area around Saumos and the Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula. It prompted large-scale precautionary evacuations of residents and summer visitors, with French emergency services using both land and maritime routes to move people and secure affected areas.

facts.label: Start and location
facts.value: The fire began around July 22, 2026, in the forested Gironde area between Saumos and Lège-Cap-Ferret, north of the Arcachon Basin on France's Atlantic coast.

facts.label: Evacuation authority and operations
facts.value: The Gironde prefecture ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula; the response involved firefighters, the Gendarmerie nationale, and evacuation by road and sea.

facts.label: Scale of displacement
facts.value: Evacuation totals changed as the fire spread, but reporting documented more than 10,000 people moved to safety on July 23 and a full-peninsula evacuation as conditions worsened.

facts.label: Return phase
facts.value: By July 30, authorities had begun allowing people back to locations they judged safe, while firefighting and safety operations continued.

facts.label: Underlying local risk framework
facts.value: Lège-Cap-Ferret is officially designated as exposed to forest-fire risk; its state-prescribed forest-fire risk-prevention plan dates from October 1, 2004, and the commune is subject to mandatory vegetation-clearance requirements.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major evacuation and wildfire developments connected to southwest France and related European fire coverage, but does not provide a complete incident log, final damage assessment, or definitive investigation findings.
